itens.titulo: Nasdaq leads Wall Street lower on AI spending jitters; oil prices rebound
itens.descricao: Nasdaq leads Wall Street lower on AI spending jitters; oil prices rebound Yahoo Finance
trechos: SpaceX dropped 3.9% and Super Micro fell 3.4% on Thursday as investors looked past earnings and weighed the soaring costs of AI investments and unclear return timeline.
Tesla fell 1.9% after the electric-vehicle maker cut annual capital expenditure forecast, raising questions about the pace of its AI and robotics ambitions.
Meta's shares slipped 6.7% after the social media giant introduced new non-voting shares to help fund its costly AI expansion.
"The thing that makes these AI names more vulnerable is just that they have such high valuations already.
So any kind of little trip up in the market is going to cause a big decline in some of these stocks," said Brendon Dashiell, portfolio manager for investment research at Bogart Wealth.
"We think markets will continue to be choppy, but we're still cautiously optimistic." Other constituents of the 'Magnificent 7' group also declined, with Amazon.com and Nvidia down about 2% each.
Intel was down 5.3%, while AMD, Qualcomm, Marvell Technology, Broadcom and Micron Technology slipped between 1.9% and 5.2%.
The renewed jitters sent the CBOE Volatility Index up 17.86 points, after three straight sessions of declines.

itens.titulo: Tesla stock slips despite Q3 earnings beat, better-than-expected capex spend
itens.descricao: Tesla stock slips despite Q3 earnings beat, better-than-expected capex spend Yahoo Finance
trechos: Tesla reported Q3 revenue of $28.05 billion vs. Bloomberg consensus of $28.13 billion.
Tesla posted adjusted EPS of $0.48 vs. the $0.44 estimate, with adjusted EBITDA of $3.90 billion vs. $3.66 billion.

Tesla stock pared some of its earlier losses, with Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein claiming the market was reacting to "capacity constraints in the company's auto and battery growth, which could slow near-term growth." But that might not be the whole story.
Tesla reported free cash flow of $1.53 billion vs. an estimated -$4.92 billion, with capital expenditures climbing to $4.732 billion vs. an estimated $7.96 billion for the quarter.
On the earnings call, Tesla updated its full-year capex guidance to $20 billion from $25 billion previously.
Tesla CFO Vaibhav Taneja said the savings would come from "managing our capital deployment efficiently, and plan to fund [capex] primarily from our cash flows from operations," he said.
"I think capex is actually ending up being a little lower than we anticipated, but we'll start to become more meaningful next year.
And then noticeable in the tens of billions in '28," CEO Elon Musk said on the call.

itens.titulo: Bitcoin Price Erases Two-Day Gains After $85,000 Rejection: Will it Fall to $80,000?
itens.descricao: Bitcoin Price Erases Two-Day Gains After $85,000 Rejection: Will it Fall to $80,000? Yahoo Finance
trechos: The Bitcoin price has erased its two-day gains after a rejection near $85,000.
Bitcoin (BTC) slid about 4% to an intraday low of $81,652 on Bybit.
On-chain data and price charts now point to $80,000 as the next key test.
Bitcoin Treasuries Sit Near Breakeven but Stopped Buying Corporate Bitcoin treasuries hold BTC at an average cost basis of about $80,000, according to Glassnode.
The price has closed above that level since September 18.
Monthly net purchases have shrunk to a few thousand BTC, far below the 2025 peaks.
A drop below $80,000 would push treasuries back underwater.
In mid-2022, a similar stretch below cost basis brought one of the only notable net sales on Glassnode's chart.

itens.titulo: Nokia's Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on AI & Cloud Strength
itens.descricao: Nokia's Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on AI & Cloud Strength Yahoo Finance
trechos: Nokia Corporation NOK reported strong third-quarter 2026 results, with both the top and bottom lines beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate.
Comparable earnings increased year over year, while revenues rose 10%, driven by robust growth in IP Networks and Optical Networks, supported by accelerating AI & Cloud demand.
The company's earnings beat the consensus estimate by 29.45%, while revenues surpassed expectations by 2.22%.
AI & Cloud net sales surged 123% on a constant currency basis, with order intake reaching €1.5 billion during the quarter.
Comparable profit from continuing operations was €498 million ($573.1 million) or €0.09 (10 cents) per share, up from €334 million or €0.06 per share in the prior-year quarter.
The bottom line beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 8 cents.
Nokia's Revenues Quarterly net sales were €5.15 billion ($5.93 billion), up 10% from €4.70 billion in the year-ago quarter.
On a constant currency basis, revenues grew 9%, primarily driven by strong AI & Cloud demand and growth in Network Infrastructure.
